sourceFiles.note: Original OT23 ODT, 16 pages. Source contains seven Story Notes, narrative teaching questions, memory-verse discussion, and ten formal review questions. ESV Isaiah 46:9b–10a is preserved as source, with a proposed BSB excerpt requiring teacher review.

storyNotes.originalText: Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat COWS being eaten by seven skinny cows.
storyNotes.cleanText: Pharaoh dreamed about seven fat cows being eaten by seven skinny cows.

storyNotes.originalText: He also dreamed of seven healthy heads of GRAIN being eaten by seven thin heads of grain.
storyNotes.cleanText: Pharaoh also dreamed about seven healthy heads of grain being eaten by seven thin heads of grain.

storyNotes.originalText: Pharaoh’s WISE men couldn’t explain the dreams. The wine taster said, “I know someone who can!”
storyNotes.cleanText: Pharaoh’s wise men could not explain the dreams. The wine taster remembered Joseph.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph was taken from PRISON, cleaned up, and sent to Pharaoh. Pharaoh told him his dreams.
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph came from prison, cleaned up, and listened to Pharaoh’s dreams.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph said, “God is showing you that Egypt will have SEVEN good years, then seven bad years.”
storyNotes.cleanText: God showed Pharaoh seven years with plenty of food, followed by seven years without enough food.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph told Pharaoh to put someone in charge of STORING up food during the seven good years.
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph told Pharaoh to choose someone to store food during the seven good years.

storyNotes.originalText: Pharaoh chose Joseph for that job. He placed Joseph SECOND in charge of all of Egypt.
storyNotes.cleanText: Pharaoh put Joseph second in charge of Egypt.

questions.question: Does anyone know the highest point on planet Earth?
questions.answer: Mount Everest.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What about the lowest place?
questions.answer: Challenger Deep, in the Pacific Ocean.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Why are we talking about the highest and lowest points of our planet?
questions.answer: The story shows Joseph going from prison to great responsibility in Egypt.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Who can remind us how Joseph ended up there?
questions.answer: Father’s favorite, given beautiful robe, hated and sold into slavery by brothers, Potiphar’s wife lied and he ended up in prison for something he didn’t do.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What did Joseph do for these men?
questions.answer: Explained what their dreams meant.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What seven things did he see?
questions.answer: He saw seven fat cows.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What did they do?
questions.answer: They ate the seven fat cows.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Do cows normally eat other cows?
questions.answer: No.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: How in the world can cannibal cows be a message from God?
questions.answer: The dreams showed seven hungry years would follow seven good years.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What happened in Pharaoh’s dream of grain?
questions.answer: First, there were seven healthy heads of grain; seven thin and sick ones came and ate the healthy ones.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: do plants swallow up other plants?
questions.answer: No.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: How were these two dreams alike?
questions.answer: They both had seven fat and healthy things that were swallowed up and eaten by seven skinny things.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: But what was God trying to say?
questions.answer: Pharaoh did not know yet; Joseph would explain that the dreams showed the next fourteen years.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: could Pharaoh’s biggest brainiacs solve the mystery of his dreams?
questions.answer: No.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Who?
questions.answer: Joseph.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review. Context: the wine taster remembered who had explained his prison dream.

questions.question: What was it?
questions.answer: To speak to Pharaoh for him and ask for help.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What did they do to make Joseph look nice and neat for Pharaoh?
questions.answer: They shaved him; changed his clothes.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: And the next?
questions.answer: He was standing before Pharaoh.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: How did Joseph respond?
questions.answer: I can’t do it, but my God can!
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: what were those seven fat things a picture of?
questions.answer: Seven good years with lots of food.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What were those seven skinny things a picture of?
questions.answer: Seven bad years where food wouldn’t grow, probably because it would stop raining.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Why would God let Pharaoh know this?
questions.answer: So Pharaoh could prepare for the years without enough food.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What did the seven skinny cows do to the fat cows?
questions.answer: They ate them.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What did the seven skinny heads of grain do with the seven fat heads of grain?
questions.answer: They ate them.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What advice did Joseph give to Pharaoh?
questions.answer: Pick a smart person; have them save up the extra food during the seven good food-filled years so they’ll have something to eat during the seven bad food-less years.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What advice did Joseph give to Pharaoh?
questions.answer: Put a smart person in charge of saving food during the seven food-filled years to eat during the seven food-less years.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Who?
questions.answer: Pharaoh.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review. Context: the only person in Egypt not required to obey Joseph.

questions.question: So how does the story of Pharaoh’s dreams teach us, strengthen us, encourage us, or give us hope?
questions.answer: It shows that God knows and rules the future.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: Because it’s his world and he’s in charge of it!
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review. Context: why God knows what will happen before it does.

questions.question: But why should we care that God knows the future?
questions.answer: Because God is never surprised and has a plan.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: is there anyone like him?
questions.answer: No.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What does that mean?
questions.answer: God can tell the future from the beginning.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: Because it’s all part of his great plan to show us his glory.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: what did God tell Pharaoh about the future?
questions.answer: There would be seven food-filled years followed by seven food-less years.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: What did they do?
questions.answer: Wash and shave him.
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim. Answer follows the original lesson; where no direct answer was supplied, it is a contextual explanation for review.

questions.question: Describe Pharaoh’s first dream.
questions.answer: Seven fat cows were swallowed by seven skinny cows
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim.

questions.question: Describe Pharaoh’s second dream.
questions.answer: Seven healthy heads of grain were swallowed by seven skinny ones
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim.

questions.question: How did Pharaoh feel about these two dreams? Why?
questions.answer: Worried because he couldn’t understand their meaning
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim.

questions.question: What happened when Pharaoh told his wise men to explain his dreams?
questions.answer: They couldn’t
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim.

questions.question: What did the wine taster say?
questions.answer: When I was in prison, a man explained my dream to me
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim.

questions.question: When Pharaoh said, “I heard you can explain dreams,” what did Joseph say?
questions.answer: God will tell me the answer
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim.

questions.question: What did the seven fat cows and seven fat heads of grain represent?
questions.answer: Seven food-filled years to come
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim.

questions.question: What did the seven skinny cows and seven skinny heads of grain represent?
questions.answer: Seven food-less years to follow
questions.notes: Original question / prompt retained verbatim.

questions.question: What advice did Joseph give to Pharaoh?
questions.answer: Put a man in charge of saving food during the first seven years to eat during the seven food-less years to follow

questions.question: What job did Pharaoh give to Joseph?

facts.statement: Pharaoh dreamed about seven fat cows and seven skinny cows.
In Pharaoh’s dream, the fat cows ate the skinny cows.
Pharaoh dreamed about healthy grain being swallowed by thin grain.
Pharaoh’s wise men could not explain his dreams.
The wine taster remembered Joseph, who had explained dreams in prison.
The baker told Pharaoh that Joseph could understand dreams.
Joseph said God could give Pharaoh the meaning of his dreams.
Joseph said Egypt would have seven hungry years, then seven good years.
Joseph told Pharaoh to save extra food during the good years.
Joseph told Pharaoh to eat up all the food during the seven good years.
Pharaoh put Joseph second in charge of Egypt.
Pharaoh sent Joseph back to prison after hearing his advice.
Pharaoh’s dreams showed that Egypt would have five good years and five bad years.
